notes: Expansion paired with grammar-replace-0020 (a single personal pronoun after a preposition takes its subject form; relation takes_case_form and the new value, the subject form, are kept). Fictional subject: a made-up class, club pronouns coined for one small club's newsletter, under the real class 'personal pronoun', restricted to the position after 'than' in a comparison, where English leaves the case open (taller than I, taller than me), so the rule fills an empty slot; the first version put the class after a preposition, where the object form is fixed, which overwrote inherited knowledge. Derived queries name made-up pronouns with their object forms in the prompt. Near unrelated: the real pronoun 'her' after the preposition 'for'; a rule that leaks to every pronoun in every position answers 'she'.
